title: the-tester-publishes-a-sealed-exec
intention: The tester publishes one way to run a shell command under its instance seal and get back its exit, stdout and stderr, so another component can run a proof-bearing instrument sealed without reaching into tester code.
why: Codemother's verdict runs every chart criterion's instrument with bash -c and no seal (cairn/devices/codemother/machines/verdict/verdict.py run_instrument), and chart instruments are `python3 <proof> | ...` (e9a2's four were). So every PROVED runs the ticket's proofs against live ~/.cairn. The tester owns the instance seal but publishes no interface to run a command under it (its charter's public_interface is empty), so the verdict cannot ask for one without reaching into tester code (RULE 1). Parent: dda0e72b9c67.
traces_to: RULE 1 (a component talks to another only through its public interface; the tester declares none today); Law 8. Parent dda0e72b9c67.
how: Add `cairn test --exec '<command>' [--timeout N]` (and the callable behind it, declared in the tester charter's public_interface) that snapshots instance space, runs `bash -c <command>` inside the same bwrap instance seal run_proof uses (instance_bind_flags over a snapshot swap, CAIRN_TESTER_INSTANCE_SEALED=1, the run marked with CAIRN_TESTER_TEST_ID), passes stdout/stderr through unchanged and exits with the command's exit code; refuses loudly (exit 2) when bwrap is unavailable rather than running bare. Proof under cairn/devices/tester/proofs/, written red.
falsifier: Done when (1) `cairn test --exec 'echo $CAIRN_TESTER_INSTANCE_SEALED'` prints 1 and exits 0; (2) a command that writes a file under ~/.cairn inside --exec leaves the live file absent afterwards; (3) the command's exit code and stdout come back unchanged (exit 3 -> exit 3, a PASS line passes through); (4) with bwrap unavailable it exits 2 naming the seal, never runs bare; (5) the tester charter's public_interface names the entry. WRONG INTENT if run_proof's existing seal path cannot run a non-proof command without duplicating it, in which case the entry wraps run_proof and the falsifier stands.
watchme: none, because (cairn/devices/tester/cli.py) --exec is a synchronous call whose refusal prints to its caller, and its seal reds via component_color on drift
children: none, because one CLI flag plus the callable behind it

chart_claim.filled_by: CC chart chain (orient 0f8398ee8eb3 .. validate f3e7590c018c, each learned)

decisions.text: The proof is already written and red: cairn/devices/tester/proofs/test_a_command_runs_under_the_seal_by_exec.py, PROVES keys 1-5 plus the composite test_the_whole_falsifier_holds_end_to_end, red 6 of 6 under the seal at 3c73e2ea. Do not edit it; build against it.
decisions.step: unlisted: write the proof red: teeth 1-5

decisions.text: Add to TesterDevice in cairn/devices/tester/device.py: def run_exec(self, command: str, *, timeout: int = 3600, cwd: str | None = None) -> int. cwd defaults to os.getcwd(); iso = get_isolation('none'). If inside_an_instance_seal(): seal = check_instance_seal(iso, _INSTANCE_ROOT, cwd), swap = _INSTANCE_ROOT if seal.sealed. Else if bwrap_available() is false: no swap. Else made = snapshot_instance_space(); seal = check_instance_seal(iso, made, cwd); swap = made if seal.sealed. Then argv = iso.wrap(['bash','-c',command], cwd=cwd, instance_swap=swap) (that is where instance_bind_flags and CAIRN_TESTER_INSTANCE_SEALED=1 come from). env = os.environ minus TEST_ID_ENV, plus TEST_ID_ENV=mint_test_id() (runs.py; env var CAIRN_TESTER_TEST_ID). subprocess.run(argv, env=env, cwd=cwd, timeout=timeout) with NO capture so stdin/stdout/stderr are the caller's; return its returncode; TimeoutExpired prints 'timed out after Ns' to stderr and returns 124. After the run, kill_what_it_started(test). finally: shutil.rmtree(Path(made).parent) when made. It mints no record and no validation.
decisions.step: unlisted: implement TesterDevice.run_exec(command, *, timeout) composing seal primitives from isolation.py

decisions.text: When no swap was confirmed (no bwrap and no inherited seal, or check_instance_seal not SEALED), run_exec prints to stderr 'cairn test --exec: refused — the instance seal is not confirmed (<verdict>: <detail>); the command was not run' and returns 2 BEFORE anything runs. Never a bare fallback.
decisions.step: unlisted: handle bwrap unavailable case - refuse with exit 2 naming the seal

decisions.text: In cairn/devices/tester/cli.py main(): ap.add_argument('--exec', metavar='COMMAND', dest='exec_command'). Change --timeout to default=None and after parsing set it to 3600 for --exec and 120 otherwise (the existing per-proof default, unchanged in meaning). Dispatch first, before reseal/hollow/discover: if args.exec_command is not None: return TesterDevice().run_exec(args.exec_command, timeout=args.timeout). fold_flags must not fold the command: after folding, put the raw token back at the index after '--exec'. Add the usage line  to the module docstring.
decisions.step: unlisted: add --exec flag to cli.py with command argument and optional --timeout

decisions.text: Through the artifact door (cairn artifact write <charter> --verb cast --why ... --from <file>), set public_interface in cairn/devices/tester/intention+why.json from [] to ["cairn test --exec '<command>' [--timeout N]  (TesterDevice.run_exec: bash -c under the instance seal; exit passes through, 2 when no seal)"]. A list of str, so the encapsulation sieve's missing_field check still holds; callers reach it by subprocess, never import.
decisions.step: unlisted: declare run_exec entry in tester charter's public_interface

decisions.text: Settled, not wrong intent: run_proof takes a proof PATH and mints a record, so it cannot run a pipeline. run_exec composes the same isolation.py primitives run_proof calls (bwrap_available, inside_an_instance_seal, snapshot_instance_space, check_instance_seal, NoIsolation.wrap) and duplicates no seal logic; run_proof is not edited.
decisions.step: unlisted: resolve WRONG INTENT precondition - confirm run_proof can run arbitrary commands without duplicating seal logic

decisions.text: D4 lost its usage line to shell quoting; the line to add under the existing usage block in cli.py is:    cairn test --exec "<command>"              run any command under the instance seal (exit passes through; 2 when no seal)
decisions.step: unlisted: add the --exec usage line to cli.py's module docstring

decisions.text: Every name D2 uses is already imported at the top of cairn/devices/tester/device.py, so add no import: from cairn.devices.tester.isolation import _INSTANCE_ROOT (the live ~/.cairn path), INDETERMINATE, Seal, bwrap_available, check_instance_seal, get_isolation, inside_an_instance_seal, snapshot_instance_space; from cairn.devices.tester.runs import ENV as TEST_ID_ENV, kill_what_it_started, mint_test_id. check_instance_seal(iso, swap_root, cwd) returns a Seal dataclass with .verdict, .detail and the .sealed property. snapshot_instance_space() returns the swap root path (str), and the caller removes its parent directory. iso.wrap(argv, cwd, *, instance_swap=) returns the argv list. test = mint_test_id() is a str, and that same value goes to kill_what_it_started(test).

fold_flags is cairn.tools.system_word.fold_flags, already imported in cli.py and called once at 'args = ap.parse_args(fold_flags(sys.argv[1:] if argv is None else argv))'. It lowercases every token that starts with '-'. Replace that line with: raw = list(sys.argv[1:] if argv is None else argv); folded = fold_flags(raw); then for i, tok in enumerate(folded): if tok == '--exec' and i + 1 < len(raw): folded[i + 1] = raw[i + 1]. Then args = ap.parse_args(folded). fold_flags itself is not edited.

Exact charter write: write the full new charter JSON (json.dumps(doc, indent=2, ensure_ascii=False) + newline) to a scratchpad file, then run: bin/cairn artifact write cairn/devices/tester/intention+why.json --verb cast --why '2c9eeab2da87: publish cairn test --exec in public_interface' --from <that file>.
